impl.head: b63425d087d2660b2ebd883da6d9975fcdb80011
impl.summary:
SPEC section 7 and the blob rows of section 13 are implemented, in two commits on wp/w1-storage: 442075e (code) and b63425d (tests plus one comment). Nothing was pushed, and no network or cloud access was used.

core/oss.py (server-side operations; presign, head, copy and delete are unchanged):
- Signing: OSS V1 Authorization header. The string to sign is VERB, Content-MD5, Content-Type, Date, the sorted and lowercased x-oss-* headers, then the canonical resource with signed subresources (a bare name when the value is empty, as in ?delete).
- put_object: sends Content-MD5. With forbid_overwrite it sends x-oss-forbid-overwrite: true and treats 409 FileAlreadyExist as success.
- get_object raises FileNotFoundError on 404. head_object_info returns size, mime, etag and last_modified, or None.
- delete_object_key does a single delete. delete_objects posts ?delete in quiet mode (XML body, application/xml, Content-MD5) in chunks of DELETE_BATCH_LIMIT = 1000.
- list_objects is ListObjectsV2 with list-type=2, prefix, max-keys, encoding-type=url and continuation-token. It parses the XML and returns (objects, next token or None).
- OssError(status, code, request_id, message) is built from the error XML, or for HEAD from the base64 x-oss-err header.
- HTTP: one pooled httpx.AsyncClient per event loop (trust_env=False, no redirects; timeouts connect 10 s, pool 30 s, default 30 s; limits 64/32, keepalive 30 s). put and get take a per-call timeout, default 120 s. close_shared_http_client() closes it at shutdown. Clients can also be injected for tests.
- The internal host (bucket.oss-{region}-internal.aliyuncs.com) is used when internal=True and the endpoint is Aliyun's.
- Credentials: cached_credentials() caches for 600 s, keyed by the credential-selecting environment variables. Failures are not cached; clear_credentials_cache() resets it. An STS token is sent as x-oss-security-token.
- get_oss() now uses the credential cache and passes the STS token along. Presigned URLs are unchanged.

trajectory/storage.py:
- BlobStore protocol (runtime_checkable).
- OssBlobStore: from_env(); cached credentials on every call; if_absent maps to forbid-overwrite; delete_prefix lists a page, then batch-deletes it.
- LocalBlobStore: writes go to a temp file in the target directory, are fsynced, then os.replace'd, followed by a best-effort directory fsync. Files are 0600, I/O runs in threads, emptied directories are pruned, and listing skips temp files.
- MemoryBlobStore: counters puts, gets, deletes and bytes; objects and content_types dicts; faults[op] per operation plus fail(op, error, times=N) and clear_faults(); an optional sync or async get_hook that runs after the read and before return.
- FaultInjectingBlobStore: probabilities from TRAJECTORY_BLOB_FAULT ('put:0.3,get:1.0,delete:0.1'), a random.Random(seed), and injected counts per operation. It raises BlobFaultInjected, a ConnectionError, never a FileNotFoundError.
- Compression: COMPRESSIBLE_TYPES and is_compressible (case-insensitive, ignores parameters). encode_blob uses zstd level 3 for compressible types of 1024 bytes or more, identity otherwise. decode_blob decodes frame by frame and raises CorruptContent on damaged input.
- Keys: blob_key, segment_key, checkpoint_key (same as blob_key), export_key, trajectory_prefix, key_prefix, check_key.
- Configuration: get_blob_store, set_blob_store and blob_store_from_env follow the section 13 defaults. Provider defaults to local, at <backend>/.openbox/trajectory-blobs. The OSS bucket and region fall back to OSS_BUCKET and OSS_REGION (read through get_config, like get_oss); the endpoint is derived from the region; the prefix defaults to trajectories/; internal defaults to true. When TRAJECTORY_BLOB_FAULT is set, the configured store is wrapped.

How the tests work:
- All HTTP goes through httpx.MockTransport.
- Every request's Authorization header is checked against a reference V1 signer written in the test from the documented algorithm; it works only from the request as sent.
- Exact string-to-sign literals are pinned for PUT with forbid-overwrite and STS, a list call with a continuation token, and POST ?delete.

Mutation check: a scratchpad pytest plugin injected one bug at a time, and every mutant made tests fail. Nothing was left in the repo.

| No signed subresources | 3 |
| x-oss headers left out of the signature | 2 |
| Delete batch size 2000 | 2 |
| Non-atomic in-place local write | 4 |
| One-shot zstd decode | 2 |
| Unseeded fault random generator | 1 |
impl.spec_deviations:
None of these contradicts the spec; each adds a guard or fills a gap:
1. get_oss(), an existing function, now uses the 10-minute credential cache and passes the STS token to the client. Section 15.1 says core/oss.py changes are additions only, but caching is required and get_oss is the module's only credential consumer. Its contract, OssNotConfigured mapping and presigned URLs are unchanged.
2. put_object returns "" when forbid_overwrite hits 409 FileAlreadyExist, because OSS does not report the existing object's ETag.
3. delete_object_key returns True for 200/204 and False for 404 (nothing to delete); other statuses raise OssError. The spec does not define the bool.
4. Failures with no HTTP answer (connect errors, timeouts) raise OssError with status 0 and the httpx exception class name as code, chained with `from`.
5. Server-side object operations reject an empty key or a key starting with / or \ with ValueError. An empty key would address the bucket itself: PUT creates a bucket, DELETE removes one. list_objects requires max_keys between 1 and 1000. An unparsable listing, or a truncated one without NextContinuationToken, raises OssError(code "InvalidResponse").
6. Key validation (check_key) applies to every store, not just LocalBlobStore, so tests share production's key space. Besides '..' (rejected as a substring), backslashes and absolute paths, it rejects NUL, drive letters, and empty, '.' or trailing-slash segments.
7. delete_prefix needs a non-empty prefix ending in '/'. An empty prefix could empty a bucket shared with user assets, and trj_1 would also match trj_10.
8. The key helpers validate their inputs: sha256 must be 64 lowercase hex characters; trajectory ids must be non-empty, contain no '/', and not start with '_' (reserved for _exports); segment ranges need 1 <= from_seq <= to_seq.
9. The phrase "relative directory for local" in section 7.2 is ambiguous. Local keys use the fixed prefix trajectories/, which matches the OSS default and the legacy local layout. TRAJECTORY_OSS_PREFIX applies only when TRAJECTORY_BLOB_PROVIDER=oss.
10. decode_blob raises trajectory.types.CorruptContent, a ValueError, for unsupported encodings, empty, truncated or invalid zstd data, and trailing garbage.
11. Fault injection has no seed environment variable; the seed is a constructor argument only. A store installed with set_blob_store is returned as given and is not wrapped.
12. head_object_info returns the keys size, mime, etag and last_modified.
13. Additive public helpers not named in the spec:
    - core.oss: cached_credentials, clear_credentials_cache, shared_http_client, close_shared_http_client, DELETE_BATCH_LIMIT, CREDENTIALS_TTL_SECONDS.
    - trajectory.storage: BlobFaultInjected, parse_blob_faults, check_key, key_prefix, is_compressible, blob_store_from_env, OssBlobStore.from_env, BLOB_OPERATIONS, DEFAULT_LOCAL_PATH.
impl.open_issues:
1. Nothing has run against a real bucket, because cloud access was prohibited. Every OSS-specific detail below comes from the documented V1 algorithm and my recollection of the SDK. It is verified only against the reference signer in the test, and no installed SDK was available to cross-check:
   - continuation-token and delete are treated as signed subresources.
   - Quiet-mode batch delete is assumed to return no per-key results.
   - HEAD error details are read from the x-oss-err header.
   - With encoding-type=url, keys and NextContinuationToken are percent-decoded.
   The first staging or drill run (w1-ops) should confirm a multi-page listing, a batch delete and a forbid-overwrite conflict.
2. The worker's shutdown (w2-service) should await core.oss.close_shared_http_client().
3. Uploads are a single PUT (OSS caps these at 5 GiB). There is no multipart upload, which would matter only if an export could exceed that.
4. LocalBlobStore's if_absent is check-then-write, not atomic like OSS forbid-overwrite. It relies on content-addressed keys and the single-writer lock (section 8.1).
5. decode_blob has no output size limit. Blobs are written only by the worker.

verify.head: 8b222f17850237e6e7c5c2879c8600b369d194ae
verify.fixes:
One commit on top of the implementer's b63425d: 8b222f1. The branch diff against feat/trajectory-rearch still touches only the 4 owned files. Nothing was pushed, and no cloud or production access was used.

Signing was checked against the real Aliyun SDK and is correct. A local cached copy of oss2 2.19.1 was found at ~/.cache/uv and its V1 signer loaded with small stubs (no network, no new dependency). It re-signed 48 requests sent by OssClient: put (plain, forbid-overwrite, STS token), get, head, delete, batch delete, and list with and without a continuation token. Keys included spaces, +, %, ~ and non-ASCII characters. 0 mismatches. It also confirmed that continuation-token and delete are signed parameters, and matched oss2 on decoding keys and tokens from a url-encoded listing and on reading the x-oss-err header. No defects in signing.

Defects found and fixed, each with a regression test. All 9 new regression tests fail when run against the pre-fix modules:

1. A wrong bucket name looked like a missing object (backend/core/oss.py). OSS answers 404 NoSuchBucket for a bucket that does not exist, and that answer was read as "no such object":
   - get_object raised FileNotFoundError, which the read path turns into "content deleted" (410).
   - head_object_info returned None, so exists() said False and a blob health check would pass.
   - delete_object_key returned False, so OssBlobStore.delete succeeded and GC would count the delete as done without removing anything.
   A new helper, _absent(), now makes these three calls raise OssError for NoSuchBucket. A 404 NoSuchKey, or a 404 with no error code, keeps the documented outcome (FileNotFoundError, None, False).
   Tests: test_a_missing_bucket_is_an_error_not_a_missing_object, test_a_coded_missing_object_keeps_the_documented_outcomes, test_oss_blob_store_reports_a_missing_bucket_instead_of_missing_objects.

2. OssBlobStore.put failed on bytearray or memoryview data, while LocalBlobStore and MemoryBlobStore accepted it. httpx raises TypeError for these types, so code tested against MemoryBlobStore would break only in production.
   - put_object now converts any bytes-like data with bytes(memoryview(data)) and rejects anything else.
   - All three stores use the same conversion. The old bytes(data) silently turned an int 7 into seven zero bytes.
   - MemoryBlobStore converts before updating its counters, so a rejected put changes nothing.
   Tests: test_put_object_accepts_bytes_like_data, test_put_object_rejects_data_that_is_not_bytes_like, test_every_store_accepts_bytes_like_data_and_rejects_the_rest.

3. LocalBlobStore left leftover bytes behind on delete (backend/trajectory/storage.py). A write killed between its temp-file write and the rename leaves a .tmp- file holding the object's bytes. delete_prefix skipped those files, so deleting or expiring a trajectory left user content on disk, and the directories could never be pruned. delete_prefix now also removes temp files under the prefix, without counting them. A write still in flight under that prefix fails and is retried by its caller. A stress script (600 concurrent puts racing 50 prefix deletes) finished with no hangs, no partial objects, nothing left under the prefix, and other trajectories untouched.
   Test: test_local_delete_prefix_removes_temp_files_of_interrupted_writes.

4. OssBlobStore.list and delete_prefix built one client, and so read credentials once, for a whole multi-page run. A slow consumer could keep signing with credentials older than the 10-minute refresh. A fresh client is now built per page.
   Test: test_oss_blob_store_signs_each_listing_page_with_current_credentials.

5. cached_credentials() returned the cached dict itself, so a caller that edited it would change what every later call signs with. It now returns a copy.
   Test: test_cached_credentials_hand_out_copies.

Test gap closed: test_signatures_match_vectors_computed_by_the_oss2_sdk pins the Authorization headers oss2 produced for a PUT with forbid-overwrite, a list with an STS token and continuation token, a batch delete and a GET of a non-ASCII key, all with a fixed Date. It also pins those requests' paths and query strings.

Reviewed and confirmed correct:
- Section 7.1: the signing layout, Content-MD5, forbid-overwrite with 409 FileAlreadyExist as success, quiet batch delete in chunks of 1000, ListObjectsV2 parsing and pagination, OssError fields, the shared httpx client (trust_env=False, explicit timeouts), internal host selection, and the 10-minute credential cache.
- Section 7.2: the BlobStore protocol, the three stores, fault injection, encode_blob/decode_blob (including skippable and empty zstd frames), and the key helpers.
- Section 13 blob settings.
- No secrets reach logs, path traversal is blocked, and the module does no database access.

verify.remaining_issues:
1. Nothing ran against a real OSS bucket; cloud access is not allowed. The staging drill (w1-ops) should confirm a multi-page listing, a quiet batch delete, a forbid-overwrite conflict and a NoSuchBucket answer, including whether HEAD sends the x-oss-err header. Two assumptions rely on the documented API and oss2's behavior: quiet mode returns no per-key errors, and NextContinuationToken arrives url-encoded.
2. backend/.openbox/trajectory-blobs, the section 13 default for local blobs, is not in .gitignore, so local dev content could be committed by accident. The legacy default (.openbox/trajectory-blobs, relative to the working directory) already had this gap. .gitignore is outside this package's ownership, so it was not changed.
3. TRAJECTORY_OSS_INTERNAL defaults to true, as section 13 says. A worker outside Aliyun's network (the AWS deployment) must set it to false, or every call goes to the unreachable intranet host. This belongs in the w1-ops runbook.
4. The worker shutdown (w2-service) should await core.oss.close_shared_http_client(). When calls come from a second event loop, the previous loop's client is dropped without being closed. That is harmless with one loop per process.
5. LocalBlobStore creates directories with the default umask (usually 0755), so trajectory ids and content hashes can be listed by other local users. Files are 0600. The spec requires 0700 only for the spool.
6. The implementer's own open issues still stand: uploads are a single PUT with no multipart (a 5 GiB limit, irrelevant with 4 MiB segments), LocalBlobStore's if_absent is check-then-write, decode_blob has no output size cap, and presigned URLs still carry no STS token (existing behavior, kept unchanged on purpose).
